title: Tate: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works in which precision, atmosphere and distortion give different forms to experience.
introduction:
The plants around Millais’s Ophelia remain insistently detailed while a body floats among them. In Turner’s storm, the difficulty is almost reversed: the surroundings make the boat hard to locate. Neither method is simply more realistic than the other. One keeps the visible world sharply available at a moment of death; the other lets weather disrupt the act of seeing itself.

This selection follows that contrast through literary subjects, city scenes and invented bodies. Some images become denser the longer they are examined. Others depend on the few details they allow to survive. The difference offers a more useful starting point than treating all looseness as spontaneity or all precision as certainty.
visitNote: Tate holds works across several sites, including Tate Britain and Tate Modern. This selection is a collection guide, not a single-building route. Check each work’s current display location before travelling; loans and installations change.

books.title: The Elements of Drawing
books.author: John Ruskin
books.note: Ruskin’s exercises in looking at natural forms offer a useful companion to the Pre-Raphaelite paintings. His attention to edges and light also gives a starting point for discussing why Turner’s surfaces are harder to separate into objects.

works.title: Ophelia
works.credit: John Everett Millais. Ophelia. Image credit: John Everett Millais. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Ophelia’s open hands and floating body occupy a stream whose vegetation is described with sustained attention. The setting does not fall out of focus around the human event. That equality of detail creates a difficult relation: the plants continue to claim the eye while the figure gives the same surroundings a fatal significance.

works.title: The Lady of Shalott
works.credit: John William Waterhouse. The Lady of Shalott. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The chain still connects the boat to the bank. Candles, patterned textile and the woman’s white dress make the departure materially specific, while her lifted face directs attention beyond the immediate action. Waterhouse holds the scene close to leaving. The consequences named by the literary subject have not yet been shown.

works.title: The Awakening Conscience
works.credit: William Holman Hunt. The Awakening Conscience. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The woman begins to rise, changing the relation between two bodies in a densely furnished room. The mirror offers another kind of opening, toward a garden and outdoor light. Hunt places the narrative turn in that small adjustment of posture, allowing an enclosing interior and a possible direction beyond it to coexist.

works.title: Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose
works.credit: John Singer Sargent. Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Warm lantern light has only a limited reach within the cooler garden. The children’s pale dresses and surrounding flowers must belong to both that localised glow and the remaining daylight. Sargent gives the scene its particular difficulty by keeping the two forms of illumination present rather than allowing one to cancel the other.

works.title: Peace: Burial at Sea
works.credit: J.M.W. Turner. Peace - Burial at Sea. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The dark sails supply weight within an atmosphere otherwise tending toward dissolution. The painting commemorates the burial at sea of Turner’s fellow painter David Wilkie, and was exhibited in 1842. That context gives the blacks a particular task: mourning is concentrated in the vessels’ appearance rather than described through a clearly legible funeral ceremony.

works.title: Norham Castle, Sunrise
works.credit: J. M. W. Turner. Norham Castle, Sunrise. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Castle, low ground and river remain recognisable with few firm edges. This unfinished painting permits light blue and yellow areas to carry relationships that detailed architecture might otherwise explain. It is useful to distinguish that surviving state from a theory of what Turner intended every passage to become: the present surface is what can be examined.

works.title: Snow Storm: Steam-Boat off a Harbour’s Mouth
works.catalogueTitle: Snow Storm - Steamboat off a Harbour's Mouth
works.credit: J. M. W. Turner. Snow Storm - Steamboat off a Harbour's Mouth. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The vessel is hard to secure within the circling marks. Sea and sky cease to provide the stable division expected in a conventional maritime view. Turner makes locating the boat part of the picture’s difficulty. The storm is described through that disruption as much as through any individually identifiable wave.

works.title: Beata Beatrix
works.credit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti. Beata Beatrix. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Closed eyes and still hands interrupt the ordinary exchange between a depicted figure and the spectator. A red bird approaches, while the warmer space behind remains less distinct. The inward state is presented through signs around the body; it is not literally opened for inspection or reducible to a single visible thought.

works.title: The Mud Bath
works.credit: David Bomberg. The Mud Bath. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Angular blue and white forms cross the red field, retaining suggestions of bodies without continuous anatomy. The group’s action survives in directions and intersections rather than individual faces. Bomberg gives a bodily subject a different scale of recognition: first a collective arrangement, then fragments from which figures may be recovered.

works.title: The Fairy Feller’s Master-Stroke
works.credit: Richard Dadd. The Fairy Feller’s Master-Stroke. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The woodcutter occupies a society so densely populated that the surrounding witnesses compete with the central action. Grasses, leaves and tiny figures overlap within shallow space. Dadd’s detail does not make the whole instantly clear. It divides attention into repeated encounters, each of which reveals how much remains outside the current focus.

works.title: The Ghost of a Flea
works.credit: William Blake. The Ghost of a Flea. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The creature has muscular weight and a walking stance, though its partly animal body refuses an ordinary human identity. Curtains give the movement a staged setting, and the carried vessel supplies a small action. Blake’s invention depends on recognisable anatomy: the departures become more definite because enough familiar structure remains.

works.title: Nocturne: Blue and Gold—Old Battersea Bridge
works.catalogueTitle: Nocturne: Blue and Gold - Old Battersea Bridge
works.credit: James Abbott McNeill Whistler. Nocturne: Blue and Gold - Old Battersea Bridge. Image credit: James McNeill Whistler; Source credit: The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN : 3936122202 .. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The bridge is a large, dark shape over water whose distances are supplied by sparse lights and a small boat. Blue and gold connect elements that are not equally described. Whistler makes the setting legible with few anchors, allowing the withheld detail to remain part of the night rather than something the spectator must complete.

works.title: Industrial Landscape
works.credit: L.S. Lowry. Industrial Landscape. WikiArt source label: L. S. Lowry Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/l-s-lowry/industrial-landscape-1955
works.license: L. S. Lowry Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Chimneys and buildings continue far beyond any one workplace. Small figures establish a human scale within their repetition, while roads connect one part of the built environment to another. Lowry treats industry as a place people inhabit, not merely a collection of machines or a single factory seen from outside.

works.title: Three Studies for Figures at the Base of a Crucifixion
works.catalogueTitle: Three Studies for Figures at the Base of a Crucifixion
works.credit: Francis Bacon. Three Studies for Figures at the Base of a Crucifixion. WikiArt source label: Francis Bacon Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/francis-bacon/three-studies-for-figures-at-the-base-of-a-crucifixion-1944
works.license: Francis Bacon Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The three panels give the creatures separate spaces but comparable orange grounds. Long necks, mouths and supports retain enough bodily information for distortion to register clearly. They share no continuous room and need not be forced into one sequential event. Repetition establishes their relation while leaving their individual predicaments distinct.

works.title: Hampstead Heath with a Rainbow
works.credit: John Constable. Hampstead Heath with a Rainbow. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The rainbow’s clear curve crosses a sky that otherwise breaks into unstable cloud and darkness. Light singles out parts of the heath below without illuminating it evenly. Constable connects separate areas through the brief arc, making weather an active redistribution of the landscape’s visibility rather than a background condition.

works.title: Self-Portrait with Badges
works.credit: Peter Blake. Self-Portrait with Badges. WikiArt source label: Peter Blake Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/peter-blake/self-portrait-with-badges-1961
works.license: Peter Blake Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The badges make selected images part of the figure’s outward appearance. They interrupt the jacket while contributing to the self-portrait’s account of identity. Face and stance remain important, but likeness is not the sole evidence. What a person wears and displays can occupy the same pictorial space as the features they were born with.

works.title: The Disrobing of Christ
works.credit: The Disrobing of Christ. WikiArt; WikiArt. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; complete source frame.
works.description: The removal of cloth requires several bodies to act in a cramped, angular space. The nearly naked figure is exposed through their handling rather than presented in isolation. Spencer keeps the sacred episode attached to awkward physical relations: fabric can conceal, connect and resist the people pulling at it.

works.title: Bursting Shell
works.credit: Christopher Richard Wynne Nevinson. Bursting Shell. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The explosion has no comfortably distant position from which to be watched. Wedges and lines radiate through the entire arrangement, carrying its force beyond a single depicted object. Nevinson gives violence a directional structure. The absence of a detailed injured body does not make the event remote when the space itself breaks apart.

works.title: Dorelia in a Black Dress
works.credit: Gwen John. Dorelia in a Black Dress. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The loosely crossed arms keep the standing pose composed without locking it into rigid symmetry. A pink accent and small changes of light distinguish the figure within a restricted range of colour. Gwen John allows the plain wall to remain plain, concentrating the encounter on face, hands and the slight adjustments of posture.

works.title: Farms near Auvers
works.credit: Vincent van Gogh. Farms near Auvers. Image credit: Vincent van Gogh; Source credit: 1. vangoghgallery.com 2. Tate Online , image. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: Thatched roofs, trees, walls and sloping ground receive marks moving in different directions. The surface stays active without making every material identical. The crowded buildings can be followed through those changes, demonstrating how a landscape may remain legible even when hardly any part of the paint settles into an uninterrupted field.

closingSections.title: Distinguish a difficult image from an unclear text
paragraphs: Dadd’s density and Turner’s disrupted visibility need different kinds of looking; neither needs vague praise in place of description. Compare what each lets remain clear. Tate is a collection presented across venues and changing displays, so check each work’s current location before planning a visit.
